proposals.before: her mother was a Shan from Henei, first cousin once removed to Grand Tutor Shan Tao.
proposals.after: her mother was a Shan from Henei, first cousin once removed to Minister over the Masses Shan Tao.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Minister over the Masses, not Grand Tutor (太傅); literal error: the office is mistranslated.

proposals.before: She died in 247 at fifty-nine and was buried at Gaoyuan mausoleum east of Luoyang; Wei later enfeoffed her posthumously as Lady of Guangping.
proposals.after: She died in 247 at fifty-nine and was buried at Gaoyuan mausoleum at Luoyang; Wei later enfeoffed her posthumously as Lady of Guangping.
proposals.reason: 葬洛陽高原陵 says only that she was buried at Gaoyuan mausoleum, Luoyang; literal error: "east of" is invented.

proposals.before: Under Wei Mingdi, Sima Yi commanded the armies while his sons showed ruthless ambition.
proposals.after: Under Wei Mingdi, Sima Yi commanded the armies while his sons all had heroic talent and grand strategic vision.
proposals.reason: 諸子並有雄才大略 praises heroic talent and grand strategy; literal error: "ruthless ambition" inverts the tone.

proposals.before: She knew Sima Yi was no loyal servant of Wei, yet as a Wei princess by birth she herself drew his deepest suspicion.
proposals.after: She knew Sima Yi was no loyal servant of Wei, yet as a maternal niece of the Wei ruling house she herself drew his deepest suspicion.
proposals.reason: 魏氏之甥 means a sister's child of the Wei (Cao) house; her mother was a Cao. Literal error: "Wei princess by birth" overstates her status.

proposals.before: her mother was a Cai from Chenliu, daughter of the Han court poet Cai Yong.
proposals.after: her mother was a Cai from Chenliu, daughter of the Han General of the Household of the Left Cai Yong.
proposals.reason: 漢左中郎將邕 gives Cai Yong's office, General of the Household of the Left; literal error: "court poet" replaces the office.

proposals.before: After Empress Xiahou died, Emperor Jing married Wu Zhi’s daughter, then divorced her, and took Yang Huiyu back; she bore no sons.
proposals.after: After Empress Xiahou died, Emperor Jing married the daughter of Wu Zhi of Puyang, General Who Guards the North; she was dismissed, and he then married Yang Huiyu; she bore no sons.
proposals.reason: 復納后 means he then married the empress (Yang); she had not been his wife before. Literal error: "took back" invents an earlier marriage and the office 鎮北將軍 was dropped.

proposals.before: Because his mother-in-law lacked posthumous honors, Emperor Wu issued in 267 an edict: “Han Wendi raised Empress Dowager Bo’s title; later Han rulers enfeoffed mothers from Pingyuan and Boping—such acts honor parents and widen kinship grace.
proposals.after: Because his mother-in-law lacked posthumous honors, Emperor Wu issued in 267 an edict: “Han Wendi conferred the posthumous title Lingwen; Emperors Wu and Xuan of Han granted the fiefs of Pingyuan and Boping—such acts honor parents and widen kinship grace.
proposals.reason: 靈文 is the posthumous title Han Wendi gave his maternal grandfather, and 武、宣 are Emperors Wu and Xuan of Han; literal error: "Empress Dowager Bo" and "mothers" misidentify the honorees.

proposals.before: Still grieving, he issued another edict: “Lady Yang, wife of former Minister Wang Lang and my maternal great-grandmother, together with my maternal uncles and my two aunts on the Zheng and Liu sides, were cherished by successive empresses.
proposals.after: Still grieving, he issued another edict: “Lady Yang, wife of former Minister Wang Lang and my maternal great-grandmother, together with my maternal uncles and my two aunts on the Zheng and Liu sides, were dearly loved by the late empress.
proposals.reason: 先后至愛 means they were the late empress's (Wang Yuanji's) dearest kin; literal error: "successive empresses" misreads 先后.

proposals.before: Her father Yang Wenzhong [2] is treated in the “Treatise on Outer Kin”;
proposals.after: Her father Yang Wenzong [2] is treated in the “Treatise on Outer Kin”;
proposals.reason: 文宗 is romanized Wenzong; literal error: "Wenzhong" misspells the name.

proposals.before: Officials asked that, as under Han custom, empress and heir each receive forty bath-fief commanderies, but the emperor refused as non-canonical.
proposals.after: Officials asked that, as under Han custom, empress and heir each receive forty counties as bath-town fiefs, but the emperor refused as non-canonical.
proposals.reason: 食湯沐邑四十縣 is forty counties (縣); literal error: "commanderies" inflates the unit.

proposals.before: Jealous by nature, she kept only plain, towering girls and rejected every truly lovely face.
proposals.after: Jealous by nature, she kept only fair-skinned, tall girls and rejected every truly lovely face.
proposals.reason: 潔白長大 means fair-skinned and tall; literal error: "plain" inverts 潔白.

proposals.before: Dying with her head on his knee she said, “Your uncle Yang Jun’s niece combines virtue and beauty—please bring her into the six palaces.”
proposals.after: Dying with her head on his knee she said, “My uncle Yang Jun’s daughter Nanyin combines virtue and beauty—please bring her into the six palaces.”
proposals.reason: 叔父駿女男胤 is "my uncle (Yang) Jun's daughter Nanyin"; literal error: "your uncle" and "niece" reverse the kinship and drop the name.

proposals.before: She longed to move her parents’ graves but, while court fashion prized austerity, stayed silent until her final hours—this wish moves us still.
proposals.after: She longed to rebury her father and grandfather but, while court fashion prized austerity, stayed silent until her final hours—this wish moves us still.
proposals.reason: 改葬父祖 is reburial of her father and grandfather; literal error: "parents" misidentifies the dead.

proposals.before: Wang Huang countered: “She conspired with Yang Jun—she cannot share Wu’s temple.
proposals.after: Sima Huang, Prince of Xiapi and Director of the Department of State Affairs, countered: “She conspired with Yang Jun—she cannot share Wu’s temple.
proposals.reason: 下邳王晃 is Sima Huang, Prince (王) of Xiapi; literal error: "Wang Huang" misreads the title 王 as a surname.

proposals.before: In Taining 316 I held the clan office; registers were gone.
proposals.after: In the second year of Taining (324) I held the clan office; registers were gone.
proposals.reason: 太寧二年 is the second year of Taining, AD 324; literal error: "316" is the wrong year.

proposals.before: Pei Yi argued Emperor Ai’s mourned empress kept mourning even after divorce.
proposals.after: The late Vice Director Pei Wei, discussing the precedent of the Mourned Empress, held that mourning for a stepmother continues even after she is cast out.
proposals.reason: 裴頠 is Pei Wei and 悼后 is Empress Wudao; literal error: "Pei Yi" misreads 頠 and "Emperor Ai" is invented.

proposals.before: Yu Yi, Yu Bing, He Chong, Zhuge Hui, Xie Guang, Liu Zhuo, Yin Rong, Feng Huai, and Deng Yi endorsed Tan—Yang Zhi joined Wu’s temple.
proposals.after: Sima Yu, Prince of Kuaiji, Yu Bing, He Chong, Zhuge Hui, Xie Guang, Liu Zhuo, Yin Rong, Feng Huai, and Deng Yi endorsed Tan—Yang Zhi joined Wu’s temple.
proposals.reason: 會稽王昱 is Sima Yu, Prince of Kuaiji; literal error: "Yu Yi" garbles the prince's name.

proposals.before: On that summer day in 274 Jin’s Empress Yang Yan passed—alas!
proposals.after: On the bingyin day of the seventh month, in autumn of the tenth Taishi year (274), Jin’s Empress Yang Yan passed—alas!
proposals.reason: 秋七月丙寅 is the bingyin day of the seventh month in autumn; literal error: "summer day" contradicts 秋 and drops the date.

proposals.before: Youxin wed Yin; Jiang water wed Zhou—inner chambers rang with virtue.
proposals.after: Youxin wed Yin; Jiang and Si married into Zhou—inner chambers rang with virtue.
proposals.reason: 姜姒 are the Zhou consorts Tai Jiang and Tai Si; literal error: "Jiang water" mistakes the names for a river.

proposals.before: Like Boyu of Zhou I ache—he wore bright robes to delight his kin.
proposals.after: Long ago Boyu, in tender devotion,—he wore bright robes to delight his kin.
proposals.reason: 昔伯瑜之婉孌兮 says "long ago Boyu, so devoted"; literal error: "of Zhou" is invented and "I ache" is not in the line.

proposals.before: Shaman Wu worked spells; healers He and Que brewed drafts.
proposals.after: Shaman Xian worked spells; healers He and Que brewed drafts.
proposals.reason: 巫咸 is Shaman Xian (咸 is his name); literal error: "Shaman Wu" renders 巫 (shaman) as a name.

proposals.before: Gentle primal queen—she widowed kindness.
proposals.after: Gentle primal queen—she truly spread kindness.
proposals.reason: 實宣慈焉 means she truly spread compassion; literal error: "widowed kindness" is a garbled rendering.

proposals.before: She shot back, “I fear death itself—why fear an emperor?”
proposals.after: She shot back, “I do not fear even death—why should I fear Your Majesty?”
proposals.reason: 死且不畏 means "I do not fear even death"; literal error: "I fear death itself" inverts the meaning.

proposals.before: She shot back, “You marched north against Gongsun and west against Zhuge—what else is warlord stock?”
proposals.after: She shot back, “Your house marched north against Gongsun and held off Zhuge in the west—what else is warlord stock?”
proposals.reason: 北伐公孫，西距諸葛 refers to the Sima house's campaigns (Sima Yi), not the emperor himself, and 距 is to resist; literal error: "You marched ... west against" misstates actor and action.

proposals.before: On xinmao in early 272 she became crown princess [7].
proposals.after: On the xinmao day of the second month of 272 she became crown princess [7].
proposals.reason: 泰始八年二月辛卯 names the second month; literal error: "early 272" drops the month.

proposals.before: Jia Mo saw danger—planned coup with Pei Yi—Wang Yan backed out.
proposals.after: Jia Mo saw danger—plotted with Pei Wei and Wang Yan to depose her—Wang Yan backed out.
proposals.reason: 裴頠 is Pei Wei and 王衍 was a co-plotter; literal error: "Pei Yi" misreads 頠 and Wang Yan's role is dropped.

proposals.before: Ill diviners forbade “Guangcheng”—she became Princess Yicheng.
proposals.after: Ill diviners forbade “Guangcheng”—her fief was changed to Yicheng.
proposals.reason: 改封宜城 means her enfeoffment was changed to Lady of Yicheng; literal error: "Princess" invents a title she did not hold.

proposals.before: Minhuai nursed her mother—deferential.
proposals.after: The empress spent more than ten days away tending her sick mother. The crown prince often visited the Yicheng residence with physicians, behaving respectfully and observing every courtesy.
proposals.reason: Corrects the actor: the empress tended her sick mother; restores the crown prince’s visits, physicians, duration and respectful observance.

proposals.before: Jiong hated her mother—Lun used him.
proposals.after: The empress had fallen out with Jiong's mother, which was why Lun sent him.
proposals.reason: Corrects the relationship: the empress had a quarrel with Jiong’s mother; restores why Lun sent Jiong.

proposals.before: May Your Majesty consult further with the Grand Tutor in depth; do not let near and far grow doubtful and draw reproach from all under Heaven."
proposals.after: May Your Majesty consult further with the Grand Steward in depth; do not let near and far grow doubtful and draw reproach from all under Heaven."
proposals.reason: 太宰 is Grand Steward (Sima Yong); literal error: "Grand Tutor" mistranslates the office.

proposals.before: Liu Yao made her consort.
proposals.after: Liu Yao usurped the throne and made her empress.
proposals.reason: 僭位，以為皇后 means he usurped the throne and made her empress; literal error: "consort" understates 皇后 and the usurpation is dropped.

proposals.before: Wu sent her to tutor him in bed—she conceived.
proposals.after: Wu sent her to the Eastern Palace to attend him in bed—she conceived.
proposals.reason: 遣往東宮侍寢 means sent to serve in his bedchamber; literal error: "tutor" is not in the text.

proposals.before: Consort attended illness ten-plus days—crown prince often visited Yicheng mansion—brought physicians—obedient exhaustive ritual.
proposals.after: The empress went out to tend her mother during her illness for more than ten days. The crown prince often visited the Yicheng residence, bringing physicians in and out and respectfully observing every propriety.
proposals.reason: Corrects the actor: the empress tended her sick mother; restores the crown prince’s visits, physicians, duration and respectful observance.

proposals.before: Consort with Jiong’s mother bore grudge—therefore Lun sent him.
proposals.after: The empress had a quarrel with Jiong's mother, so Lun sent him.
proposals.reason: Corrects the relationship: the empress had a quarrel with Jiong’s mother; restores why Lun sent Jiong.

proposals.before: Zhao Can, Jia Wu, Han Shou, Dong Meng executed.
proposals.after: Zhao Can, Jia Wu, Han Shou, Dong Meng and the others were all executed.
proposals.reason: Restores all four named individuals, the others and explicit execution; removes unsupported compression that they died with the empress.

proposals.before: Her cabal died with her.
proposals.after: Zhao Can, Jia Wu, Han Shou, Dong Meng and the others were all executed.
proposals.reason: Restores all four named individuals, the others and explicit execution; removes unsupported compression that they died with the empress.

decisions.after: her mother was a Shan from Henei, a paternal grand-aunt by cousinship of Minister over the Masses Shan Tao.
decisions.reason: s0041 司徒濤之從祖姑 names Tao as 司徒, not 太傅. 從祖姑 is a collaterally senior aunt of the grandfather’s generation (as the sealed literal already has), not “first cousin once removed.” The proposed office fix is kept; the kinship wording is aligned with the Chinese.
s0052 葬洛陽高原陵 locates the burial at Gaoyuan mausoleum in Luoyang and does not say east of the city. Removing the invented direction is required.
s0060 諸子並有雄才大略 praises heroic talent and grand strategy. “Ruthless ambition” inverts the Chinese.
s0061 后既魏氏之甥, with s0058 母曹氏, makes her a sister’s child of the Cao house, not a Wei princess by birth.
s0068 漢左中郎將邕 states Cai Yong’s office. “Court poet” is not in the Chinese and must be replaced.

s0070 更娶鎮北將軍濮陽吳質女，見黜，復納后: after Jinghuai’s death he married Wu Zhi’s daughter, she was dismissed, then he took in this empress. “Took back” invents a prior marriage to Yang Huiyu; 鎮北將軍 and 濮陽 belong in the line.
s0092 漢文追崇靈文之號，武、宣有平原、博平之封 names the title 靈文 and Han emperors Wu and Xuan with those fiefs. “Empress Dowager Bo” and “mothers from Pingyuan and Boping” are not in the Chinese.
s0148 先后至愛 is love from the late empress, not successive empresses. The rest of the proposed sentence already matches 外曾祖母故司徒王朗夫人楊氏 and 鄭、劉二從母.
s0154 父文宗 is Wenzong. The sealed person record also uses 文宗 / Wenzong; Wenzhong is a romanization error.
s0677 食湯沐邑四十縣 is forty counties, not commanderies.
s0164 惟取潔白長大: 潔白 is fair-skinned, not plain.
s0172 叔父駿女男胤 is the speaker’s uncle Yang Jun’s daughter named 男胤. “Your uncle” and “niece” reverse the kinship and drop the name.
s0177 改葬父祖 is reburial of father and grandfather, not both parents. s0176 already distinguished 二親.
s0248 尚書令、下邳王晃: 王 is the princely title of 下邳, not a surname. The sealed person is Sima Huang, Prince of Xiapi, holding 尚書令.

decisions.after: In the second year of Taining I held the clan office; registers were gone.
decisions.reason: s0265 太寧二年 is the second Taining year, so “316” is wrong. The host after inserts AD 324, which is not in the Chinese; this revision restores 太寧二年 without an unsupported Western year.
s0274 故尚書僕射裴頠議悼后故事，稱繼母雖出，追服無改: the man is Pei Wei, the case is 悼后, and no Emperor Ai appears.
s0282 會稽王昱 is Sima Yu, Prince of Kuaiji, not Yu Yi. The remaining names match the Chinese list.
s0317 泰始十年秋七月丙寅 is autumn, seventh month, day bingyin, not a summer day. The proposal restores those Chinese calendar elements.
s0318 姜姒 are the two Zhou consorts Jiang and Si, not “Jiang water.”

decisions.after: Long ago Boyu, in tender devotion, wore bright robes to delight his kin.
decisions.reason: s0300 昔伯瑜之婉孌兮，每綵衣以娛親 has no Zhou and no “I ache.” The host after is accepted in substance; the broken “devotion,—he” punctuation is repaired.
s0383 巫咸: 咸 is the shaman’s name. Rendering 巫 as the name “Wu” is wrong.
s0452 實宣慈焉 is that she truly spread kindness, not “widowed kindness.”
s0498 死且不畏，何畏陛下 inverts if rendered as fearing death.
s0507 北伐公孫，西距諸葛: 距 is to hold off, and the campaigns belong to the Sima house invoked as 將種, not to the reigning emperor marching in person.
s0532 泰始八年二月辛卯 names the second month; “early 272” drops it.
s0559 乃與裴頠、王衍謀廢之，衍悔而謀寢: 頠 is Wei, and Wang Yan is a named co-plotter who then withdrew.
s0576 改封宜城 changes the enfeoffment to Yicheng. 君 is not 公主; “Princess” is invented.
s0577 后出侍疾十餘日，太子常往宜城第，將醫出入，恂恂盡禮: the empress went out to nurse; the heir visited with physicians. “Minhuai nursed her mother” names the wrong actor and drops the rest.
s0588 后與冏母有隙，故倫使之: the empress had a quarrel with Jiong’s mother, which is why Lun sent him. The before reverses who hated whom.
s0630 太宰 is not 太傅. Grand Steward is the supported office in this memorial.
s0639 曜僭位，以為皇后: usurpation and empress rank are both explicit; “consort” understates 皇后.

decisions.after: Wu, worried the crown prince was still young and did not know the affairs of the bedchamber, sent her to the Eastern Palace to attend him in bed—she conceived.
decisions.reason: s0653 武帝慮太子尚幼，未知帷房之事，乃遣往東宮侍寢，由是得幸有身. The host after correctly removes “tutor” and restores 東宮, but still omits the motive 尚幼 / 未知帷房之事, which the Chinese states.
s0577 literal must name the empress as the one who 出侍疾 and keep the heir’s visits with physicians, matching the idiomatic repair.
s0588 literal 后與冏母有隙 matches the idiomatic correction of actor and motive.
s0599 趙粲、賈午、韓壽、董猛等皆伏誅 names four people, 等, and 伏誅. The before dropped 等皆.
s0599 idiomatic “Her cabal died with her” invents death-with-the-empress and omits all four names and 伏誅.

claimRetractions.reason: s0576 改封宜城 does not create a princess. The English name Princess Yicheng is invalidated by r0027; c1963 already records 宜城君 as Lady of Yicheng.
s0172 駿女男胤 is Yang Jun’s daughter named 男胤, not a niece. The descriptive-kinship English “niece” is invalidated by r0012; c1245 already records parent-of / 女.

claimRevisions.reason: s0154 文宗 is Wenzong; the English personal-name Wenzhong is a romanization error corrected with r0009.
s0248 下邳王晃 is the Prince of Xiapi, not a man surnamed Wang. English title Wang Huang is invalidated by r0014.
s0274 裴頠 is Pei Wei, not Pei Yi.
s0282 會稽王昱 is Sima Yu, Prince of Kuaiji, not Yu Yi.
s0383 巫咸: 咸 is the name. English Shaman Wu is invalidated by r0021.
s0559 裴頠 is Pei Wei, not Pei Yi.

proposals.before: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.
proposals.after: Earlier, Empress Jia's mother, Guo Huai, had wanted Han Shou's daughter to become crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry into the Han family to strengthen his position.
proposals.reason: Restores Han Shou’s name, his daughter, Guo Huai’s relationship to Empress Jia, the crown-princess proposal and the crown prince’s motive.

proposals.before: Guo Huai once pushed a Han match—Yu wanted it too.
proposals.after: Earlier, Empress Jia's mother, Guo Huai, had wanted Han Shou's daughter to become crown princess. The crown prince also hoped that marrying into the Han family would strengthen his position.
proposals.reason: Restores Han Shou’s name, his daughter, Guo Huai’s relationship to Empress Jia, the crown-princess proposal and the crown prince’s motive.

decisions.reason: s0034 literal already has 賈后母郭槐, 韓壽女, 太子妃, and 太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固. The proposed after is stylistic only and does not restore omitted content.
s0034 idiomatic “Guo Huai once pushed a Han match—Yu wanted it too” omits 韓壽, 韓壽女, 賈后母, 太子妃, and 以自固. The proposed after restores those Chinese elements.

proposals.before: Mi was then Attendant of the Yellow Gate; when he came to the Eastern Palace the Heir Apparent sometimes dismissed him and played in the rear court.
proposals.after: Mi was then Palace Attendant; when he came to the Eastern Palace the Heir Apparent sometimes dismissed him and played in the rear court.
proposals.reason: Corrects the office 侍中 to Palace Attendant; preserves the existing actions and subjects.

proposals.before: Mi was then Attendant of the Yellow Gate. When he visited the Eastern Palace the heir apparent sometimes dismissed him and amused himself in the rear court.
proposals.after: Mi was then a Palace Attendant. When he visited the Eastern Palace the heir apparent sometimes dismissed him and amused himself in the rear court.
proposals.reason: Corrects the office 侍中 to Palace Attendant; preserves the existing actions and subjects.

decisions.reason: s0152 謐時為侍中 is Palace Attendant. “Attendant of the Yellow Gate” is the wrong office.
s0152 idiomatic has the same 侍中 error; Palace Attendant is the supported rendering, and the visit / dismissal / rear-court actions are already correct.

claimRevisions.reason: s0152 侍中 is Palace Attendant, not Attendant of the Yellow Gate. Invalidated by r0032/r0033.

additionalRepairs.before: her mother was a Shan of Henei, a paternal grand-aunt by cousinship of Minister of Education Tao.
additionalRepairs.after: her mother was a Shan of Henei, a paternal grand-aunt by cousinship of Minister over the Masses Shan Tao.
additionalRepairs.reason: s0041 司徒濤 is the same 司徒 office as the idiomatic repair; “Minister of Education” and the dropped surname Shan should not remain on the literal field.

additionalRepairs.before: When Empress Jinghuai died, Emperor Jing further married the daughter of Wu Zhi of Puyang, General Who Guards the North; she was dismissed; he took in the empress again; she had no sons.
additionalRepairs.after: When Empress Jinghuai died, Emperor Jing further married the daughter of Wu Zhi of Puyang, General Who Guards the North; she was dismissed; he then took in the empress; she had no sons.
additionalRepairs.reason: s0070 復納后 is the subsequent marriage of this empress after Wu Zhi’s daughter was dismissed. Literal “again” invents the same prior marriage that r0006 removes from the idiomatic field.

additionalRepairs.before: Lady Yang, widow of General Wang Su, Marquis Jing of Lanling, bore inward grace and outward modesty, fulfilled every womanly virtue, linked great houses by marriage, and observed the three obediences without fault.
additionalRepairs.after: Lady Yang, wife of the late General Who Guards the Army, Marquis Jing of Lanling, bore inward grace and outward modesty, fulfilled every womanly virtue, linked great houses by marriage, and observed the three obediences without fault.
additionalRepairs.reason: s0093 故衛將軍、蘭陵景侯夫人羊氏 does not name Wang Su. That name is unsupported in this unit.

additionalRepairs.before: Her father Wenzhong [2]—see the “Treatise on Outer Kin”;
additionalRepairs.after: Her father Wenzong [2]—see the “Treatise on Outer Kin”;
additionalRepairs.reason: s0154 父文宗. The idiomatic Wenzhong repair must be matched on the literal field.

additionalRepairs.before: The offices memorialized that, following Han precedent, the empress and crown prince should each receive forty commanderies as bath-and-maintenance fiefs, but the emperor held this was not ancient practice and did not permit it.
additionalRepairs.after: The offices memorialized that, following Han precedent, the empress and crown prince should each receive forty counties as bath-and-maintenance fiefs, but the emperor held this was not ancient practice and did not permit it.
additionalRepairs.reason: s0677 四十縣. The same commandery/county error remains on the literal field after r0010.

additionalRepairs.before: At the end, pillowing on the emperor’s knee she said: “Uncle Yang Jun’s niece has virtue and beauty; I beg Your Majesty to keep her for the six palaces.”
additionalRepairs.after: At the end, pillowing on the emperor’s knee she said: “My uncle Yang Jun’s daughter Nanyin has virtue and beauty; I beg Your Majesty to keep her for the six palaces.”
additionalRepairs.reason: s0172 叔父駿女男胤. The literal still has niece and drops 男胤 after the idiomatic repair.

additionalRepairs.before: Also she had in mind wishing to reburial father and grandparents; because recent affairs strove to esteem thrift, at first she did not speak; drawing near to death’s agony she stated this intent—the feeling also pities her.
additionalRepairs.after: Also she had in mind wishing to rebury her father and grandfather; because recent affairs strove to esteem thrift, at first she did not speak; drawing near to death’s agony she stated this intent—the feeling also pities her.
additionalRepairs.reason: s0177 改葬父祖 is father and grandfather, not grandparents. The ungrammatical “wishing to reburial” is corrected with the same Chinese.

additionalRepairs.before: Minister Director Prince Kang of Xiapi Huan and others debated: “The empress dowager secretly plotted with Jun to overturn the state—she cannot again serve the temple or pair with the late emperor.
additionalRepairs.after: The Director of the Department of State Affairs, Sima Huang, Prince of Xiapi, and others debated: “The empress dowager secretly plotted with Jun to overturn the state—she cannot again serve the temple or pair with the late emperor.
additionalRepairs.reason: s0248 尚書令、下邳王晃. Literal “Prince Kang of Xiapi Huan” invents Kang and misreads 晃. The idiomatic repair names Sima Huang; the literal must match.

additionalRepairs.before: I also saw former Minister Director Pei Yi’s opinion on Empress Dao’s case—though a stepmother had departed, mourning obligations stayed unchanged.
additionalRepairs.after: I also saw the late Vice Director Pei Wei’s opinion on the Mourned Empress’s case—though a stepmother had been cast out, mourning obligations stayed unchanged.
additionalRepairs.reason: s0274 尚書僕射裴頠議悼后故事. Literal Pei Yi and Empress Dao repeat the errors r0016 removes from the idiomatic field.

additionalRepairs.before: Prince Hui of Kuaiji Yu, Palace Supervisor Yu Bing, Palace Director He Chong, Minister Director Zhuge Hui, Minister Xie Guang, Superintendent of the Household Liu Zhuo, Intendant of Danyang Yin Rong, Defender-general Feng Huai, and Palace Rider Deng Yi all followed Tan’s opinion; thereby the dowager shared Emperor Wu’s sacrifices.
additionalRepairs.after: Sima Yu, Prince of Kuaiji, Palace Supervisor Yu Bing, Palace Director He Chong, Minister Director Zhuge Hui, Minister Xie Guang, Superintendent of the Household Liu Zhuo, Intendant of Danyang Yin Rong, Defender-general Feng Huai, and Palace Rider Deng Yi all followed Tan’s opinion; thereby the dowager shared Emperor Wu’s sacrifices.
additionalRepairs.reason: s0282 會稽王昱. Literal “Prince Hui of Kuaiji Yu” garbles the same name r0017 corrects in the idiomatic field.

additionalRepairs.before: Ancient Youxin married Yin; Jiang Si returned to Zhou—virtue spread within the palace, fair fame forever flows.
additionalRepairs.after: Ancient Youxin married Yin; Jiang and Si married into Zhou—virtue spread within the palace, fair fame forever flows.
additionalRepairs.reason: s0318 姜姒 are two consorts. Literal “Jiang Si” as one person repeats the collapse r0019 removes from the idiomatic field.

additionalRepairs.before: Fang replied: “North you attacked Gongsun—west you resisted Zhuge—if not general stock, what?”
additionalRepairs.after: Fang replied: “North your house attacked Gongsun—west it held off Zhuge—if not general stock, what?”
additionalRepairs.reason: s0507 北伐公孫，西距諸葛 is the Sima house’s campaigns invoked as 將種; 距 is to hold off. The literal still makes the reigning emperor the campaigner and is aligned with r0024.

additionalRepairs.before: Mo knew consort fierce—feared disaster reaching himself—with Pei Yi and Wang Yan plotted deposition—Yan repented—plot slept.
additionalRepairs.after: Mo knew the consort was fierce—feared disaster reaching himself—and with Pei Wei and Wang Yan plotted her deposition—Yan repented—the plot slept.
additionalRepairs.reason: s0559 裴頠. Literal Pei Yi is the same misreading r0026 corrects in the idiomatic field.

additionalRepairs.before: She faked pregnancy—snatched Han Shou’s son Weizu—called him newborn heir.
additionalRepairs.after: At first she feigned pregnancy, hid straw goods as birthing gear inside, then took her sister’s husband Han Shou’s son Weizu and raised him, claiming he had been born in the mourning period, and therefore did not show him openly.
additionalRepairs.reason: s0571 后詐有身，內稿物為產具，遂取妹夫韓壽子慰祖養之，託諒闇所生，故弗顯. The idiomatic line omits 妹夫, the birthing gear, 養之, 諒闇, and 故弗顯.

additionalRepairs.before: Sima Lun sent Liu Hong with golden liquor.
additionalRepairs.after: Lun then forged an edict dispatching Minister Liu Hong and others, bearing a tally, to deliver gold-filings wine and grant the empress death.
additionalRepairs.reason: s0597 倫乃矯詔遣尚書劉弘等持節齎金屑酒賜后死. The idiomatic line omits 矯詔, 尚書, 等, 持節, 金屑酒, and 賜后死.

additionalRepairs.before: Wish Your Majesty deeper consult Grand Mentor—do not let far near doubt—invite slander realm-wide.”
additionalRepairs.after: Wish Your Majesty deeper consult the Grand Steward—do not let far near doubt—invite slander realm-wide.”
additionalRepairs.reason: s0630 太宰. Literal Grand Mentor is the same 太傅 error r0030 removes from the idiomatic field.

additionalRepairs.before: Jia Wu and the empress forced Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng instead.
additionalRepairs.after: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused, and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.
additionalRepairs.reason: s0035 而壽妻賈午及後皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍小女惠風. The idiomatic line drops 壽妻, turns 不聽 into “forced,” and omits that the betrothal was for the crown prince.

additionalRepairs.before: Mi slandered the heir apparent to the empress, saying: "He hoards private wealth to win over petty men because he means to destroy the Jia clan."
additionalRepairs.after: Mi slandered the heir apparent to the empress, saying: "The heir apparent amasses private wealth to win over petty men because of the Jia clan."
additionalRepairs.reason: s0155 太子多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也 states the cause as 為賈氏故也. “Means to destroy the Jia clan” is not in this sentence.
